definitions.explanation: polite term for customer, patron, or guest; the standard respectful term used by businesses and service providers to address or refer to customers

examples.japanese: お{客様|きゃくさま}、ご{注文|ちゅうもん}は{以上|いじょう}でよろしいですか。
examples.english: Customer, is that all for your order?

examples.japanese: お{客様|きゃくさま}の{声|こえ}を{大切|たいせつ}にしています。
お{客様|きゃくさま}は{神様|かみさま}です。
examples.english: The customer is god. (Customer is always right.)

notes:
HONORIFIC TERM:
お{客様|きゃくさま} is the standard honorific term for customers in business contexts. It combines the honorific prefix お～ with {客|きゃく} (guest/customer) and the honorific suffix ～{様|さま}.

FORMALITY LEVELS:
- お{客様|きゃくさま} - most polite (business standard)
- お{客|きゃく}さん - polite (casual business)
- {客|きゃく} - neutral/plain

COMMON PHRASES:
- お{客様|きゃくさま}{各位|かくい} - dear customers (written)
- お{客様|きゃくさま}サービス - customer service
- お{客様|きゃくさま}の{声|こえ} - customer feedback/voice
- お{客様|きゃくさま}センター - customer center

CULTURAL NOTE:
「お{客様|きゃくさま}は{神様|かみさま}です」(The customer is god) is a famous Japanese saying reflecting the emphasis on customer service.
